THESE MFAs HAVING BEEN HEARD AND RESERVED FOR JUDGMENT ON 07.02.2023, COMING ON FOR PRONOUNCEMENT OF JUDGMENT THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:-
 JUDGMENT
Though these appeals are listed for admission, with the consent of learned counsel for the parties the same is taken up for final disposal.

2. These two appeals filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short) are arising out of judgment and award dated 07.11.2018 in M.V.C.No142/2018, whereby the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by petitioner and granted compensation in a sum of Rs.5,22,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. and directed respondent No.1 to pay the same.

3. While MFA No.200154/2019 is filed by respondent No.1 - NEKRTC with a prayer to set aside the impugned judgment and award and dismiss the petition or alternatively to modify the same by reducing the compensation, MFA No.201258/2019 is filed by petitioner/claimant to enhance the compensation.
4. Since these two appeals are arising out of the same judgment and award, they are clubbed together and are decided by a common order.
5. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
6. FACTS: It is the case of the petitioner that on 06.07.2017, petitioner was waiting for bus at Yanniwadgera bus stop.
When NEKRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-33- F-0055 ('the offending vehicle' for short) came and he was boarding the same
, suddenly the driver of the bus moved it in a high speed and as a result of which, petitioner lost balance and fell down.
The rear wheels of the bus touched the petitioner, who suffered simple and grievous injuries.
Despite prolonged treatment and spending Rs.3,00,000/- towards treatment, he is not completely cured.
The injuries has resulted in permanent partial disability.
At the time of accident, petitioner was aged 18 years.
In addition to being a student, he was earning Rs.8,000/- and assisting his family members.
After the accident, he lost income and prays to allow the petition and grant him compensation in a sum of Rs.17,00,000/-.
7. Respondent No.1 is the NEKRTC and respondent No.2 is the driver of the offending vehicle.
They have filed separate written statement contending that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
The offending vehicle was already moving when the petitioner tried to enter into the same and slipped and fell down and sustained injuries.
In order to make wrongful gain, he has made false claim.
They have disputed that at the time of accident, the petitioner was aged 18 years and in addition to being a student, he was helping his family members and earning Rs.8,000/- per month.

sentences.text: 3 To claim higher compensation, petitioner is falsely claiming so.
He has sustained simple injuries and they have not resulted in disability and prays to dismiss the petition.
8. Based on these pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.
9. In order to prove his case, petitioner got examined himself as PW-1 and two Doctors as PWs-2 and 3.
He has relied upon Exs.P-1 to P-15.
10. On the other hand, on behalf of Respondents, the Conductor and driver of the offending vehicle are examined as RW-1 and RW-2 and Ex.R-1 is marked.

11. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition holding that at the time of the accident, petitioner was aged 17 years and relying upon the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Master Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager National Ins.
Co. Ltd & Anr.,1 it has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.5,22,000/- including the (2014) SCC 396 medical expenses.

sentences.text: It has rejected the contention of the petitioner that at the time of accident, he was a major and earning Rs.8,000/- per month.

The details of compensation granted are as under:
Heads Amount  In Rs.
 Compensation as per Master 3,00,000 Mallikarjun's case  Pain and suffering 21,000  Loss of amenities 20,000
Medical expenses 1,81,225  Total 5,22,225  Rounded off to 5,22,000 12.
During the course of arguments, learned counsel for petitioner submitted that as per SSLC Marks Card at Ex.P-12, at the time of accident, petitioner was aged 18 years.

Therefore, the Tribunal ought to have applied multiplier method instead of relying on the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Master Mallikarjun's case, which is applicable to children below the age of 18 years.
In the light of the evidence of the PWs-2 and 3, the Tribunal ought to have taken permanent partial disability at 65% to the left pelvis and 36% to the lower urinary tract.
The Tribunal has erred in considering the permanent partial disability at 25% only.
The compensation granted under other heads is also on the lower side and prays to enhance the compensation by allowing the petition.

13. On the other hand, learned counsel representing respondent Nos.1 and 2 submitted that as per the evidence of PW-2, the disability assessed is at 20% to the whole body and as per the evidence of PW-3, the disability of particular organ is at 36%.
Therefore, the Tribunal has erred in considering the whole body disability at 25%.

Since petitioner has also contributed towards the cause of accident, the compensation ought to have been reduced proportionately and prays to allow the M.D Nekrtc Central Office vs Revansiddayya S/O Gurubasayya ...

14. Heard elaborate arguments and perused the record.
15.

Having regard to the fact that petitioner is claiming to be 18 years age at the time of accident, it is necessary to examine what exactly was the age of the petitioner at the time of accident and whether the Tribunal is justified in applying Master Mallikarjun's case in determining the compensation.
Ex.P-12 is the SSLC Marks Card of the petitioner.
According to this document, his date of birth is 23.03.2000.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, he was aged about 16 years 8 months and 17 days.
Therefore, the Tribunal is justified in considering him as below the age of 18 years and applying Master Mallikarjun's case.
In the light of the SSLC Marks Card, it does not lie in the mouth of the petitioner that as on the date of accident, he had completed 18 years.
Moreover, petitioner has not lead any evidence to show that in addition to pursuing his studies, he was also earning.

Except saying that he was assisting his family members, petitioner has not stated what exactly was the business or avocation followed by his family members and in what way he was able to assist them and earn Rs.8,000/- per month.

It appears only for the purpose of claiming higher compensation,
petitioner has come up with such a false contention, which he has failed to substantiate.

Therefore,
the findings of the Tribunal that he had not completed the age of 18 years and therefore, applying Master Mallikarjun's case cannot be interfered with.
16. So far as the nature of the injury and quantum of compensation to which the petitioner is entitled is concerned, petitioner has examined PW-2 Dr.V.M. Ghawalkar.
He has assessed the disability of the petitioner as 20% of the whole body.
PW-3 Dr. Dajendra Kothari has assessed the disability suffered by the petitioner as 36% of the particular organ i.e., lower urinary tract.
Therefore, on overall assessment of the evidence of PWs-2 and 3, the Tribunal has rightly considered the whole body disability at 25%.
It does not call for interference by this Court.

In Master Mallikarjun's case, while dealing with the death or personal injury of a child, in a motor vehicle accident, the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "in case of accident of a child resulting in disability, it would be it would be unfair and improper to follow the structured formula as per the Second Schedule.
The main stress in structured formula is on pecuniary damages.

For children,
there is no income.
A child cannot be equated to a non-earning person as done in Second Schedule taking notional income at Rs.15,000/- per year.

Therefore, the compensation is to be worked out under the non- pecuniary head in addition to the actual amount incurred for treatment done and/or to be done, transportation, assistance of attendant, etc."

It further held that "In addition to treatment, attendant etc., the following compensation is to be granted for disability of whole body (unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick):
 i) Upto 10% - Rs.1,00,000/-
 ii) 10% to 30% - Rs.3,00,000/-

Central Office vs Revansiddayya S/O Gurubasayya ... on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141413166/

5 17. Keeping reliance in Master Mallikarjun's case, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- under the head pain and suffering already undergone and to be suffered in future, mental and physical shock, hardship, inconvenience and discomfort etc., and loss of amenities in life on account of the permanent disability.

Though after granting compensation in a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- as per Master Mallikarjun's case, the Tribunal is not required to grant any separate compensation under the head Pain and suffering and loss of amenities of life, the Tribunal has granted Rs.21,000/- and Rs.20,000/- respectively under these two heads which is liable to be disallowed.

Based on medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted a compensation of Rs.1,81,225/-
and the same is upheld.
However, the Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head 'inconvenience to the parents'.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.20,000/- is granted under the head 'inconvenience to the parents'.
Similarly, the Tribunal has not granted any compensation under the head 'diet and nourishment etc.,'.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.21,000/- is granted under this head.

Thus,
in all, petitioner is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.5,22,225/- which is rounded off to Rs.5,22,000/- by the Tribunal.
The details of the compensation is as detailed below:

Heads Amount Amount  granted by granted by  the Tribunal this Court in  in Rs. Rs.
 Compensation as per 3,00,000 3,00,000  Master Mallikarjun's  case  Pain and suffering 21,000 -  Loss of amenities 20,000 -  Medical expenses 1,81,225 1,81,225  Inconvenience to the - 20,000  parents  Diet and nourishment - 21,000  etc.,
 Total 5,22,225 5,22,225  Rounded off to 5,22,000 5,22,000 18.

In the result, both appeal fails and accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
(i) Both appeals filed by the petitioner and respondent No.1 are rejected.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is hereby confirmed.

(iii) The respondent No.1 is directed to pay the compensation in a sum of Rs.5,22,000/-

(v) The amount in deposit (if any) shall be transmitted to the Tribunal.
(vi) The Registry is directed to send back the trial Court records along with copy of this judgment to the Tribunal forthwith.
